evidence.excerpt: SIMULATED, not announced by Stripe: GET /v1/payment_intents/{intent} response.amount (units_changed, currency scope USD): USD amount in minor currency units (cents): 1000 represents $10.00 -> USD amount in major currency units (dollars): 10 represents $10.00. Published schema unchanged (integer).

Equivalent fixtures stripe.payment_intents.usd-whole-dollars.baseline -> stripe.payment_intents.usd-whole-dollars.proposed: pi_demo_10usd 1000 -> 10 (USD $10.00); pi_demo_4000usd 400000 -> 4000 (USD $4,000.00); pi_demo_5000usd 500000 -> 5000 (USD $5,000.00); pi_demo_6000usd 600000 -> 6000 (USD $6,000.00); pi_demo_25eur 2500 -> 2500 (EUR 25.00 (outside the USD scope; unchanged))

Amount intended to be collected by this PaymentIntent. A positive integer representing how much to charge in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal) (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The minimum amount is $0.50 US or [equivalent in charge currency](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#minimum-and-maximum-charge-amounts). The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).

Executable scenario available, not yet run: GET /v1/payment_intents/{intent} through the official stripe-python SDK: review_payment flags USD $6,000.00 (pi_demo_6000usd) for manual review and flags neither $4,000.00 nor exactly $5,000.00, for both the baseline responses (USD minor units: 600000/400000/500000) and the equivalent SIMULATED proposed responses (USD major units: 6000/4000/5000).
